title: el1xr_opt: an open-source optimization model for the design and operation of hybrid renewable energy systems
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: el1xr_opt is an open-source mixed-integer linear optimization model, built in Pyomo, that co-optimizes the sizing (investment) and the operation of hybrid renewable energy systems coupling electricity and hydrogen. It includes unit commitme
content: el1xr_opt is an open-source mixed-integer linear optimization model, built in Pyomo, that co-optimizes the sizing (investment) and the operation of hybrid renewable energy systems coupling electricity and hydrogen. It includes unit commitment, storage dynamics, a pressure-resolved hydrogen network with compression, and frequency containment reserve (FCR) provision with endurance and response-speed constraints. It extends the openTEPES modelling framework and ships automatic solver setup. This archived release also bundles the reproducibility dataset for the study “Market-driven co-sizing of a hybrid power–hydrogen virtual power plant for energy and frequency reserve markets” (Alvarez, Gutierrez-Guerra, and Ramos) under data/H2VPPFCR/: the 2025 SE3 market series (day-ahead, FCR-N and FCR-D capacity prices, activation duties), the ERA5 site wind, the hydrogen-demand profiles, the techno-economic parameters, the case builder, and the experiment configurations. Every case in the paper regenerates from these inputs against this model version.

title: Hybrid Power Solution in West Africa Offshore Shallow Water Projects
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Reliable power supply for remote unmanned offshore wellhead platforms (WHPs) remains a recurring challenge in shallow- water West Africa, where long submarine power imports and diesel-only generation can be difficult to justify tec
content: Abstract Reliable power supply for remote unmanned offshore wellhead platforms (WHPs) remains a recurring challenge in shallow- water West Africa, where long submarine power imports and diesel-only generation can be difficult to justify technically, economically, and environmentally. This paper presents a pre-FEED engineering framework developed for the HOBA WHP in the Niger Delta to enable a renewable-dominant power architecture based on solar photovoltaic (PV), small wind turbines, nickel-cadmium (Ni-Cd) battery energy storage, and a standby diesel generator. The study combines site-specific resource screening, technology benchmarking against comparable offshore hybrid deployments, and a ground-up load rationalization process tailored to unmanned operations. The most important design step was not equipment selection, but demand reduction: the preliminary analogous-platform load basis of approximately 130 kW was reduced to about 65 kW total platform load, while the continuous unmanned demand was reduced from 14.46 kW to 6.37 kW. This load optimization reduced the indicative PV deck area requirement from approximately 600 m2 to about 200 m2 and made a hybrid offshore concept physically feasible within the WHP footprint. Long-term resource screening indicates that the project location has sufficient solar irradiation to make PV the dominant daytime energy source, while low-to-moderate coastal wind provides complementary night-time and cloudy-period support. The resulting concept adopts a DC-centric power architecture with multi-day battery autonomy and a standby diesel generator reserved for manned campaigns and contingency operation. The paper demonstrates that hybrid solar-wind-battery systems can be technically credible for small, unmanned shallow-water platforms in West Africa, provided that the design is anchored in disciplined load rationalization, realistic metocean data, and integration with platform layout and operations philosophy. The workflow is repeatable for similar WHPs seeking lower emissions, lower logistics exposure, and improved lifecycle resilience.

title: Renewable Energy Landscape and the Challenge of Gas Development in Nigeria
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Nigeria's energy landscape is characterized by a heavy dependence on oil and gas, with natural gas representing a critical component of the country's energy mix. However, despite being one of the largest producers of natural gas in
content: Abstract Nigeria's energy landscape is characterized by a heavy dependence on oil and gas, with natural gas representing a critical component of the country's energy mix. However, despite being one of the largest producers of natural gas in Africa, Nigeria has struggled with issues such as inadequate infrastructure, regulatory challenges, and inconsistent policies that hamper gas development and its integration into the national energy framework. The potential for natural gas to play a transformative role in Nigeria's energy transition is significant, given its cleaner-burning characteristics compared to coal and oil, coupled with the urgency to ameliorate power supply challenges that affect millions of Nigerians. This paper examined the dynamics of Nigeria's transition towards a gas-based sustainable energy system, exploring the opportunities and challenges presented by the development of its gas resources. It investigated the extent to which gas can contribute to energy security, economic stability, and environmental sustainability, particularly in comparison to other energy transition models globally. Through this investigation, the paper derived insights that inform policy decisions and strategic initiatives in Nigeria's quest for a comprehensive energy transition. To guide this inquiry, the following research questions were formulated: What are the current barriers to gas development in Nigeria? How can natural gas contribute to improving energy access and sustainability in the country? What lessons can be learned from the experiences of other nations pursuing similar energy transitions? By addressing these questions, the paper endeavors to contribute to the ongoing discourse on energy policy and transition in Nigeria, offering empirical insights and theoretical contributions that can aid stakeholders in navigating this complex landscape. Key findings indicate that while Nigeria possesses immense potential in solar, wind, hydro, and biomass resources, policy inconsistencies, financing constraints, infrastructure deficits, and entrenched fossil fuel interests have limited large-scale deployment. Natural gas development remains central to Nigeria's energy and industrial policy, particularly under initiatives such as the "Decade of Gas" (2021–2030) strategy. However, this focus has inadvertently diverted resources and political will away from renewable deployment. The report concludes that achieving a sustainable balance between gas and renewables requires targeted reforms to governance, incentives, and infrastructure planning. A just and inclusive energy transition in Nigeria must integrate gas as a short-term stabilizer while systematically scaling up renewable investments, technology localization, and public-private collaboration to achieve net-zero emissions by 2060.

title: Pyrolysis of Algae for Bio Oil Production
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract The increasing concentration of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) and the environmental challenges associated with fossil fuel dependence necessitate the development of sustainable alternatives. This research investigates the pyroly
content: Abstract The increasing concentration of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) and the environmental challenges associated with fossil fuel dependence necessitate the development of sustainable alternatives. This research investigates the pyrolysis of Chlorella vulgaris algae as a means for Bio-oil production. The study involved cultivating microalgae under controlled conditions, preparing the biomass, and subjecting it to pyrolysis at 550 °C. The products were characterized using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX), and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR). Results showed that the algae biomass possessed favorable properties for pyrolysis, yielding between 175 ml and 350 ml of Bio-oil per 1000 g of feedstock. However, the flash point values (65–78°C) and sulfur content levels (0.784–0.833 wt%) of the Bio-oil samples fell below international biodiesel standards (ASTM D6751 and EN 14214), indicating the need for upgrading. This study concludes that although algae-derived Bio-oil requires further refinement, it presents a viable and renewable energy source for mitigating fossil fuel dependence and addressing environmental pollution, particularly in regions like Nigeria.

title: State-Adaptive Autonomous Drone Systems for Energy Infrastructure Inspection
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract The increasing use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in energy-sector operations- such as pipeline inspection, infrastructure monitoring, and remote asset surveillance- has highlighted critical limitations in predominantly manual
content: Abstract The increasing use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in energy-sector operations- such as pipeline inspection, infrastructure monitoring, and remote asset surveillance- has highlighted critical limitations in predominantly manual and semi-automated drone systems. While current UAV deployments offer improved safety and efficiency over traditional inspection methods, their dependence on continuous human control and stable communication links restricts scalability, resilience, and operational autonomy in complex or hazardous environments. This paper presents a conceptual framework for (state) adaptive autonomous UAV systems designed to address these limitations. The proposed approach emphasizes the integration of intelligent sensing, perception, decision-making, control, and communication as coordinated layers capable of adjusting to changing operational conditions. Rather than focusing on specific implementations, the framework outlines how autonomy-driven design principles can enhance UAV reliability, reduce human intervention, and improve operational continuity in energy-sector applications. By positioning autonomy as a critical enabler rather than an optional feature, this work aligns with ongoing digital transformation and energy transition efforts. The paper discusses potential application scenarios within oil and gas, power infrastructure, and renewable energy systems, and highlights key challenges related to regulation, system validation, and future deployment. The proposed framework provides a foundation for further research and development toward resilient, intelligent UAV operations in the evolving global energy landscape.

title: Decarbonizing Nigeria's Midstream: Stability Analysis of Hybrid Wind-Gas Power for Remote Pipeline Assets
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Nigeria's remote pipeline pump stations experience over 4,000 hours of power outages annually due to chronic grid instability, with available capacity often limited to 38-40% of installed generation, forcing operators to rely heavi
content: Abstract Nigeria's remote pipeline pump stations experience over 4,000 hours of power outages annually due to chronic grid instability, with available capacity often limited to 38-40% of installed generation, forcing operators to rely heavily on high-emission standby generators. To address this challenge, this study proposes a decentralised 10 MW wind-gas hybrid power architecture designed to deliver reliable power to unmanned midstream facilities while aligning with the IRENA 2023 Renewable Energy Roadmap for Nigeria. The system combines wind generation with an industrial gas turbine to ensure continuous power supply under variable operating conditions. The hybrid system was modelled in MATLAB/Simulink R2023a to evaluate dynamic frequency response and governor stability under fluctuating wind speeds. The gas turbine governor was modelled to maintain a nominal frequency of 50 Hz within a ±2.5% tolerance, while a supervisory SCADA-based Power Management System provided real-time monitoring and automated control. Wind resource inputs were obtained from the Global Wind Atlas 3.0, focusing on northern Nigerian pipeline corridors where grid reliability is weakest. The SCADA framework functions as an autonomous control layer, rapidly adjusting turbine output to compensate for wind intermittency and prevent frequency excursions. Simulation results indicate that the proposed architecture can reduce annual CO2 emissions at such facilities by 21-35% compared with conventional gas-only power systems, depending on wind capacity factor (21% at CF…35%; 35% at CF…45%+). The Power Management System effectively mitigates frequency spikes by instantaneously ramping gas turbine output, preventing nuisance trips and protecting sensitive equipment. Economically, the system achieves a full hybrid LCOE of $0.063/kWh, the wind generation component alone is $0.042/kWh, while eliminating the logistical and security challenges associated with diesel fuel transportation to remote locations. By integrating renewable generation directly with turbine control and SCADA automation, this study presents a software-validated engineering framework tailored to the operational realities of Nigeria's midstream infrastructure. While existing literature often addresses general grid stability, this research focuses on the synchronisation between engine controls and SCADA systems necessary to manage renewable volatility in unmanned environments. By addressing the specific tension between national decarbonisation goals and the operational constraints of remote petroleum infrastructure, this study provides a scalable and technically robust pathway for decarbonising remote petroleum assets.

title: Assessing Geothermal Energy Resources in Nigeria for Sustainable Energy Development
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Geothermal energy in Nigeria represents a promising renewable energy source capable of providing reliable baseload electricity and direct heat applications while supporting decarbonisation and net-zero objectives. Unlike solar and
content: Abstract Geothermal energy in Nigeria represents a promising renewable energy source capable of providing reliable baseload electricity and direct heat applications while supporting decarbonisation and net-zero objectives. Unlike solar and wind energy, which are intermittent by nature, geothermal systems provide a stable and continuous energy supply, making them ideal for integration into national power grids and industrial operations. Nigeria has several potential geothermal resources, including hot springs, sedimentary basins, and depleted hydrocarbon and abandoned oil and gas wells. Despite the presence of geological indicators and features in various parts of the country, geothermal energy development and deployment in Nigeria remains limited. This study investigates Nigeria's geothermal energy potential, focusing on the distribution of resources, the characteristics of the geology and reservoirs, and suitable energy conversion pathways and technologies in shallow and deep geothermal systems. The methodology is based on a comprehensive assessment and systematic analysis of the existing geothermal resources and their thermal characteristics, integrated with Heat in place (HIP) and Monte Carlo simulations. Geothermal resources are classified as shallow, deep, or associated with abandoned oil and gas wells, and each resource category is evaluated in terms of its geothermal energy potential and the suitability of available energy conversion technologies. The findings indicate significant geothermal resource potential in Nigeria, with estimated hydrothermal geothermal resources of approximately 430 MJ associated with thermal springs, 20 GJ from sedimentary geothermal systems, and 220 MW of potential energy recoverable from abandoned wells, based on Heat in place (HIP) and Monte Carlo simulations. Thermal springs and abandoned wells present immediate opportunities for low to medium temperature applications, such as direct heat use and small-scale energy systems. In contrast, sedimentary (deep geothermal) systems represent a longer-term prospect for electricity generation due to their greater development requirements and investment needs. The findings also highlight critical research gaps that must be addressed to support future geothermal development in Nigeria. Addressing these challenges will be essential for positioning geothermal energy as a key component of Nigeria's diversified renewable energy portfolio, thereby enhancing energy security, promoting sustainable economic development, and contributing to climate change mitigation efforts.

title: Revolutionizing Midstream Operations: Cutting-Edge Technologies for Enhanced Efficiency, Safety, and Sustainability
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract The midstream sector is essential for transporting and storing petroleum, acting as a crucial link between upstream production and downstream delivery. Nonetheless, conventional midstream operations are encountering growing challen
content: Abstract The midstream sector is essential for transporting and storing petroleum, acting as a crucial link between upstream production and downstream delivery. Nonetheless, conventional midstream operations are encountering growing challenges regarding safety, efficiency and environmental effects. This paper investigated the latest technological innovations that are reshaping midstream infrastructure, promoting operational excellence and ensuring sustainability over the long term. The study begun with a summary of midstream functions, highlighting the importance of innovation to enhance processes and reduce risks. Significant advancements in pipeline technologies were then analyzed, including networks equipped with sensors, systems for real time monitoring and predictive maintenance driven by artificial intelligence (AI). These innovations improve pipeline integrity, decrease failure rates and avert expensive leaks, thereby ensuring a more robust energy supply chain. The study then examined innovations in storage facilities, such as automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS), IoT-enabled tank monitoring and advanced materials for constructing tanks. These technologies maximize capacity, lessen the need for manual operations and enhance safety protocols, resulting in improved operational efficiency. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) was also discussed, with uses in predictive analytics for equipment upkeep, forecasting demand and risk management. By utilizing AI-driven insights, midstream operators can diminish downtime, reduce expenses and optimize resource distribution. Lastly, the paper highlights sustainability initiatives, featuring the implementation of renewable energy-operated pump stations, carbon capture technologies and environmentally friendly materials. These advancements align with global efforts to decarbonize and strengthen the industry's commitment to minimizing its environmental impact. By presenting these pioneering advancements, this paper emphasizes the transformative capacity of technology in modernizing midstream operations. The findings illustrate how innovation is not only boosting efficiency and safety but also preparing the midstream sector for a more sustainable future in a changing energy landscape.

title: Policy and Regulatory Drivers of Hybrid Energy System Deployment in Oil and Gas
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract With a growing focus on sustainable oil and gas energy use, hybrid energy systems are gaining interest as they integrate renewable sources of energy with traditional fossil fuel-based energy generation. Previous studies have focuse
content: Abstract With a growing focus on sustainable oil and gas energy use, hybrid energy systems are gaining interest as they integrate renewable sources of energy with traditional fossil fuel-based energy generation. Previous studies have focused largely on the technical performance and efficiency of hybrid energy systems, but relatively little has been studied on policy and regulatory aspects that affect their implementation in oil and gas operations. The impact of policy and regulatory environment on the deployment of hybrid energy system in the oil and gas sector was the subject of this study, and a particular study was conducted in Nigeria. Research was conducted using a mixed method approach which included a structured review of literature, comparative analysis of energy policies and key stakeholder engagement. A literature review was conducted to find suitable analytical frameworks for energy policy assessment, regulatory impact analysis and energy integration. These encompassed policy score card comparison, regulatory gap analysis and determination of effectiveness of incentives to assess hybrid energy policies in Nigeria. The policy instruments were evaluated according to their clarity, efficacy in enforcement, and their compatibility with the environmental goals and the operational context of the oil and gas industries. The analysis of hybrid energy policies was informed and validated by engaging with policymakers, energy regulators and industry practitioners. The study highlighted the role of the regulatory instruments (e.g. FITs, fiscal measures, carbon credit mechanisms, renewable portfolio standards) in promoting the use of hybrid energy as well as issues faced in the implementation of policies, regulatory uncertainties and integration with existing infrastructure for oil and gas. The study placed the concept of hybrid energy policy into the context of Nigeria's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), with a focus on the need for regulatory clarity and effective implementation of energy policies to ensure that hybrid energy systems are deployed effectively in the oil and gas sectors. Overall, the study suggested that a move toward the implementation of a more coherent regulatory framework and better policy implementation is needed to advance the use of hybrid energy systems in the oil and gas sector, closing the gap between the technical potential for implementation and the execution of policy.

title: Geopolitical Shocks and National Petroleum Policy: Lessons for Nigeria from the Russia-Ukraine Crisis
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract The Russia–Ukraine conflict, which began on 24 February 2022, triggered the most severe energy market disruption since the 1970s, pushing Brent crude above $139 per barrel and exposing underlying weaknesses in petroleum-reliant eco
content: Abstract The Russia–Ukraine conflict, which began on 24 February 2022, triggered the most severe energy market disruption since the 1970s, pushing Brent crude above $139 per barrel and exposing underlying weaknesses in petroleum-reliant economies. This paper leverages the crisis as a natural experiment in geopolitical shock transmission, with Nigeria—Africa's foremost crude producer—as the primary case, employing time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) volatility-connectedness analysis. The TVP-VAR method is chosen because it tracks how spillovers between variables change over time, detecting shifts and irregularities in these connections that fixed models miss – giving a clearer picture of how volatility spread before, during, and after the war shock. The results reveal persistently high total connectedness, averaging approximately 73–76%, meaning most of the ups and downs in any variable come from the others. Global energy prices act as the main source of shocks, while Nigeria's production and exports mainly receive them. The analysis identifies three structural policy shortcomings worsened by the shock, which are; long-term underperformance of state-owned refineries, leading to near-total dependence on imported refined products despite extensive rehabilitation efforts; decline of traditional export markets as key buyers shifted to discounted Russian crude; and unsustainable escalation of fuel subsidy expenditure amid surging international refined product prices. As a result, Nigeria's output stayed below OPEC targets, creating an ongoing export gap. Europe met the same challenge with the ambitious REPowerEU programme, investing €300 billion in shared energy purchases and fast-tracked renewables. Nigeria, by comparison, stuck mostly to temporary solutions such as expanded subsidies and currency adjustments instead of deeper fixes. The paper outlines a practical four-part reform plan to build better defences against similar future disruptions and ease the shift to a changing energy future. Putting these in place would help Nigeria better manage sudden global crises and advance toward lasting economic progress.

title: Leveraging Abandoned Oil Wells for Geothermal Energy: A Techno-Economic Pathway to Nigeria's Energy Transition
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract The oil and gas industry remains Nigeria's dominant energy provider; however, global pressures for cleaner and more sustainable sources highlight the urgency of national energy diversification. One promising pathway is the repurpos
content: Abstract The oil and gas industry remains Nigeria's dominant energy provider; however, global pressures for cleaner and more sustainable sources highlight the urgency of national energy diversification. One promising pathway is the repurposing of abandoned oil and gas wells for geothermal energy production, an approach that leverages existing subsurface infrastructure while significantly reducing the cost of new drilling. This opportunity could attract investment, enhance energy security, and reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Yet, the technical and economic viability of such systems in Nigeria remains largely underexplored, creating a critical knowledge gap this paper aims to address. This study develops a conceptual closed-loop geothermal system for abandoned Niger Delta wells. Wells were screened based on depth, temperature gradient, casing, and integrity; three representative cases were selected for thermo-economic modeling. A downhole U-tube heat exchanger with an insulated return leg was modeled, and multiple working fluids were evaluated for heat extraction efficiency, pumping requirements, and suitability for local geothermal conditions. The economic assessment considers well status (suspended, temporarily, or permanently plugged), including retrofitting costs, CAPEX, OPEX, surface facility costs, and levelized cost of energy (LCOE) for both direct-use and electricity generation applications. This approach enables a comparative assessment of technical and economic viability across case wells. Preliminary modeling indicates that the conceptual closed-loop geothermal system can deliver produced fluid temperatures of 131°F-167°F, sufficient for direct-use heating and low-temperature power generation. Economic analysis shows that retrofitting suspended or temporarily plugged wells is most cost-effective, with a modeled LCOE of 120-180 $/MWh and levelized cost of heat of 25-45 $/MWh. Overall, this study presents a pragmatic approach for turning decommissioning liabilities into useful energy assets while providing cleaner energy alternatives. However, widespread deployment will depend on supportive policies and integration into national renewable energy plans to enable commercial adoption.

title: Laboratory Simulation of Serpentinization Processes for Sustainable Hydrogen Production
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Serpentinization; the hydration of ultramafic rocks represents a natural mechanism for abiotic hydrogen generation with potential renewable energy applications. This study simulates serpentinization reactions under controlled labor
content: Abstract Serpentinization; the hydration of ultramafic rocks represents a natural mechanism for abiotic hydrogen generation with potential renewable energy applications. This study simulates serpentinization reactions under controlled laboratory conditions to evaluate the effect of temperature, pressure, and mineral composition on hydrogen yield. Synthetic olivine (Mg2SiO4) samples were reacted with deionized water in a high-temperature and high-pressure reactor at 80 - 200 °C and 1-5 MPa for 72 h. The formation of serpentine and brucite phases was confirmed via X-ray diffraction and FTIR analysis. Gas chromatography results indicated measurable hydrogen evolution, with the maximum production rate of 2.8 mmol H2 kg−1 rock h−1 at 120 °C, 3 MPa, and pH 9.5. Reaction kinetics followed a pseudo–first-order model, showing a strong correlation (R2 = 0.96) with temperature-dependent rate constants. These findings suggest that low temperature serpentinization can produce hydrogen at rates comparable to natural ultramafic systems, highlighting its potential as a sustainable geological hydrogen source.

title: Energy Policy Pathways for Balancing Hydrocarbon Production, Energy Transition, and Renewable Integration in Nigeria's Oil and Gas Sector
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Nigeria's oil and gas sector is central to its economy but faces rising decarbonization pressure. The country's electricity system is 82% gas-dependent yet severely underutilized, with energy-sector emissions reaching ~109 MtCO₂ in
content: Abstract Nigeria's oil and gas sector is central to its economy but faces rising decarbonization pressure. The country's electricity system is 82% gas-dependent yet severely underutilized, with energy-sector emissions reaching ~109 MtCO₂ in 2024 at one of the world's highest emissions intensities. This study evaluates pathways balancing hydrocarbon production, energy transition, and renewables integration. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study analyzes energy data (2015–2024) and key policies, including the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 and the Energy Transition Plan (ETP) 2022, and models four scenarios to 2030 and 2050. Installed capacity grew from 10,395 MW in 2015 to 13,365 MW in 2024, still dominated by gas (81.9%). Gas flaring fell from 18.8% to 7.7%, yet 192 BCF flared annually represents significant waste. Scenario modelling shows a Hybrid Pathway combining strategic gas expansion with accelerated renewables as the most feasible. The Accelerated Renewables scenario offers the lowest long-term emissions but requires over 100% annual solar growth and $8-10 billion in investment. Recovering flare gas could generate nearly 3 GW of power while cutting emissions by up to 6 MtCO₂ annually. Policy tensions exist between the PIA's gas incentives and the ETP's net-zero targets. Institutional fragmentation across five agencies compounds delays, evidenced by the gap between flare site awards and operational projects. The study concludes Nigeria's transition hinges on hydrocarbon-renewable hybridization, with gas as a bridge. Key recommendations include creating a transition coordination council, dedicating 5-10% of hydrocarbon revenues to a transition fund, and integrating flare gas recovery with power infrastructure planning.

title: The Role of Biomethane in the Energy Transition: Pathways, Economics, and Future Prospects
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Modern bioenergy, especially in the forms of biogas and biomethane, has become the most significant renewable energy source worldwide, accounting for 55% of renewable energy and over 6% of global energy consumption. Consistent with
content: Abstract Modern bioenergy, especially in the forms of biogas and biomethane, has become the most significant renewable energy source worldwide, accounting for 55% of renewable energy and over 6% of global energy consumption. Consistent with the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario, bioenergy is anticipated to play an essential role in replacing fossil fuels by 2030. Biogas can be used in various ways, such as for local heating and in Combined Heat and Power (CHP) systems, while biomethane acts as a direct alternative to natural gas, supporting circular economy initiatives and promoting sustainable energy solutions. Our research centers on converting biogas to biomethane by eliminating impurities, mainly CO2, to enhance methane levels. The upgrading methods encompass several technologies, including water scrubbing, chemical scrubbing, physical scrubbing, pressure swing adsorption, and membrane separation. The adaptability of biomethane allows it to be utilized in the transportation sector as fuel, as a natural gas substitute in heating applications, and for off-site CHP units. The costs of producing biomethane vary between €25/MWh and €100/MWh, positioning it as a financially competitive option against fossil gas in Europe. This cost leads to a hydrogen production expense of €0.83 to €3.33 per kg, which is considerably lower than the cost of producing green hydrogen through electrolysis (€4/kg, with hopeful estimates ranging from €1-2/kg). Considering current market dynamics, biomethane is likely to remain more economically attractive than green hydrogen for the near future. The consistent growth in bioenergy usage, averaging an annual increase of 7% from 2010 to 2021, highlights its increasing importance in the energy transition. Unlike hydrogen, biomethane benefits from a pre-existing distribution network, facilitating its widespread implementation. A robust political environment is crucial to foster the expansion of the renewable gas sector. By incorporating biogas and biomethane into global energy frameworks, we can improve energy security, encourage sustainability, and hasten the move toward a net-zero emissions future.

title: Simulation and Optimization of an Off-Grid Solar–Hydropower Hybrid System for Sustainable Rural Electrification in Rivers State, Nigeria
source: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
summary: Abstract Energy conservation and sustainable power supply remain critical challenges in rural communities of Rivers State, Nigeria, where electricity access is limited by weak grid infrastructure, dispersed settlements, and high dependence
content: Abstract Energy conservation and sustainable power supply remain critical challenges in rural communities of Rivers State, Nigeria, where electricity access is limited by weak grid infrastructure, dispersed settlements, and high dependence on costly and environmentally harmful diesel generators. These constraints result in inefficient energy use, high operational costs, and unreliable electricity supply. Addressing these challenges, this study presents a simulation and optimization of a solar–hydropower hybrid energy system for a rural community in Rivers State, with particular emphasis on energy conservation through efficient resource utilization and reduced system losses. The study employs HOMER Pro Micro-grid software to model and analyze an off-grid hybrid system integrating photovoltaic (PV) and mini-hydropower resources. The software enables comprehensive assessment of technical performance, economic viability, and energy efficiency, while optimizing component sizing to minimize excess generation and fuel dependency. Community load demand, renewable resource availability, and system costs are used as key inputs for the simulation. Results indicate that a hybrid hydro–PV configuration provides a reliable and energy-efficient solution for rural electrification, significantly reducing reliance on diesel generation and improving overall energy conservation. The optimized system demonstrates low cost of energy, reduced operational expenses, and enhanced sustainability through effective exploitation of locally available renewable resources. By balancing solar and hydropower generation, the system ensures stable electricity supply while conserving energy and minimizing environmental impact. The findings highlight the suitability of decentralized hybrid renewable energy systems as a viable strategy for energy conservation and rural electrification in Rivers State. This study provides valuable insights for policymakers, researchers, and energy planners seeking sustainable, cost-effective, and energy-efficient solutions for underserved rural communities.

title: An interpretable metaheuristic-optimized RVFL architecture for robust CO₂ emissions prediction in decarbonizing energy systems
summary: Abstract Sustainable energy transition requires accurate forecasting tools to guide decarbonization and environmental policy. This study develops an artificial intelligence-based framework to predict CO₂ emissions in Germany using advanced
content: Abstract Sustainable energy transition requires accurate forecasting tools to guide decarbonization and environmental policy. This study develops an artificial intelligence-based framework to predict CO₂ emissions in Germany using advanced machine learning techniques. The proposed model integrates a Random Vector Functional Link network with the Whale Optimization Algorithm to enhance learning efficiency, optimize hyperparameters, and improve predictive performance. The analysis uses monthly data from 1990 to 2021 and incorporates key drivers of environmental development, including renewable energy consumption, economic growth, financial development, globalization, and geopolitical risk. The optimization process significantly reduces the need for manual parameter tuning and strengthens model robustness. The results show strong contemporaneous prediction (nowcasting) accuracy, with an out-of-sample R² of 0.9978, outperforming conventional machine learning benchmarks. However, under expanding-window validation, the proposed model, together with every benchmark, exhibits substantial performance deterioration across structural breaks, which is a limitation of the current study. To ensure transparency and application relevance, SHAP-based interpretability analysis evaluates the contribution of each variable. The findings reveal that renewable energy expansion plays the most significant role in reducing CO₂ emissions, confirming its central importance in Germany’s decarbonization strategy. Economic and financial factors also influence emissions dynamics, highlighting the interconnected nature of energy and economic systems. The study demonstrates how artificial intelligence can enhance data driven decision making in sustainable development. It provides a useful nowcasting predictive and interpretability tool for energy planning and environmental management under stationary conditions, while underscoring the need for regime-aware methods when the data-generating process shifts.

title: Meta-heuristic optimization of PWM techniques for advanced multilevel inverter applications: A review of Selective Harmonic Elimination (SHE) Strategies
source: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
summary: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are the converter topology of choice for medium- and high-power applications, including renewable energy integration, motor drives, and flexible AC transmission systems, owing to their ability to synthesize near-
content: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are the converter topology of choice for medium- and high-power applications, including renewable energy integration, motor drives, and flexible AC transmission systems, owing to their ability to synthesize near-sinusoidal output voltage with lower switching losses and reduced electromagnetic interference compared with two-level converters. Among the modulation strategies used to control MLIs, Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (SHE-PWM) remains the preferred low-switching-frequency technique because it offers direct, deterministic control over specific low-order harmonics while maximizing the fundamental output voltage. However, the SHE-PWM problem reduces to a system of nonlinear transcendental equations that becomes increasingly difficult to solve as the number of inverter levels and therefore the number of switching angles — increases. Classical iterative solvers such as the Newton-Raphson method and algebraic approaches based on resultant theory are highly sensitive to initial guesses and become computationally prohibitive at higher levels. This has motivated an extensive body of research applying meta-heuristic optimization algorithms including Genetic Algorithms, Particle Swarm Optimization, Differential Evolution, Ant Colony Optimization, Artificial Bee Colony, Cuckoo Search, Bat Algorithm, Grey Wolf Optimizer, Whale Optimization Algorithm, Salp Swarm Algorithm, Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization, and numerous hybrid variants to solve the SHE-PWM angle-computation problem without requiring an analytical or near-optimal initial guess. This review consolidates and critically examines this literature: it presents the mathematical formulation of the SHE-PWM problem with explicit governing equations, illustrates the underlying staircase waveform and the generic meta-heuristic solution workflow through diagrams, offers a comparative discussion of algorithm families and their reported performance in terms of total harmonic distortion (THD), convergence behaviour, and computational burden, and consolidates this comparison into descriptive and attribute-based tables. Persistent research gaps — including limited real-time embedded implementation, inconsistent benchmarking practices, and insufficient treatment of asymmetric and reduced-switch-count topologies are identified, and future research directions are proposed.

title: The Subsea Climate Paradox: Thermal Pollution, Electromagnetic Disruption, and Grid Weaponization in Transoceanic HVDC Infrastructure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: As global decarbonization mandates accelerate alongside the unprecedented power demands of artificialintelligence (AI) compute infrastructure, transoceanic High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) subsea power gridsare increasingly advocated as a
content: As global decarbonization mandates accelerate alongside the unprecedented power demands of artificialintelligence (AI) compute infrastructure, transoceanic High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) subsea power gridsare increasingly advocated as a solution to regional energy intermittency. Proponents argue that cross-bordersubsea cables can wheel renewable electricity across continents, balancing global supply and demand. Thispaper presents a critical framework demonstrating that the transoceanic subsea grid paradigm introduces fatalphysical, ecological, and geopolitical contradictions—a phenomenon defined here as the Subsea ClimateParadox.1. Physically, resistive power loss over multi-thousand-kilometer subsea lines converts underwater conduitsinto high-capacity marine radiators, generating localized thermal pollution in benthic zones. 2. Ecologically, the resulting high-intensity anthropogenic Electromagnetic Fields (EMF) blindfold electro-receptive and geomagnetic marine fauna, disrupting vital migratory and foraging corridors. 3. Geopolitically, reliance on real-time subsea power imports exchanges traditional storable energydependencies for immediate "kill-switch" vulnerabilities, exposing host nations to catastrophic grid sabotageand state-level extortion.We conclude that transoceanic subsea power networks represent an unsustainable transfer of terrestrial energyburdens onto fragile marine ecosystems and national security frameworks. Policy and capital must shift awayfrom transoceanic grid expansion toward sovereign, high-density, 24/7 baseload power generation—specificallyterrestrial and floating Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and Power-to-X (P2X) chemical energy carriers.

title: Cyber-Physical Security of Renewable Energy Microgrids: A State-of-the-Art Review of Threats, Standards and Research Gaps for Sub-Sahara Africa
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Renewable energy microgrids are critical particularly to rural electrification and energy- access in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where well over 600 million people lack reliable power (IEA, 2023). These cyber-physical systems integrate solar,
content: Renewable energy microgrids are critical particularly to rural electrification and energy- access in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where well over 600 million people lack reliable power (IEA, 2023). These cyber-physical systems integrate solar, wind, storage, and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) control, making them vulnerable to both cyber and physical attacks. This review examines the current threat landscape, existing standards, and research gaps for securing renewable microgrids in Sub -Sahara Africa. We examined 61 studies from 2017-2025 and found that SSA microgrids face rather very unique risks like legacy devices, poor connectivity, insider threats, and limited incident response capacity. While standards like IEC 62443 and NIST CSF exist, adoption in SSA is still relatively low due to cost and skills gaps. We propose a context-aware security framework combining lightweight cyber defenses, physical hardening, and community governance. Future and prospective research need to prioritize low-cost intrusion detection, secure protocols for low-bandwidth links, and policy alignment with national energy strategies.

title: Instability of Antimony‐Based Energy Storage Materials in Alkaline Environments
summary: Effective energy storage is crucial for maintaining a reliable supply of renewable energy. Supercapacitors serve as buffers, storing surplus energy during low demand and releasing it during peak times. Antimony‐based materials are promising
content: Effective energy storage is crucial for maintaining a reliable supply of renewable energy. Supercapacitors serve as buffers, storing surplus energy during low demand and releasing it during peak times. Antimony‐based materials are promising candidates for supercapacitors due to their high‐power density and long cycle life. This study demonstrates that, although antimony‐based materials have previously been investigated in alkaline electrolytes, antimony sulfide iodide (SbSI), antimony sulfide (Sb 2 S 3 ), and antimony oxide (Sb 2 O 3 ) exhibit extremely poor stability in alkaline electrolytes such as NaOH and KOH. They react with these solutions to form compounds such as potassium antimony sulfide oxide (K 3 SbS 3 ·(Sb 2 O 3 ) 3 , PASO), which compromise supercapacitor performance. Although initially stable, PASO degrades quickly upon cycling, affecting long‐term storage applications. The study further investigates the stability of SbSI in different electrolytes through cyclic voltammetry, such as in neutral 0.5 M Li 2 SO 4 and acidic 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 electrolytes. SbSI shows improved structural stability in the acidic environment, while in the neutral electrolyte, its electrochemical response is less effective due to polarization and poor charge storage. These findings highlight the importance of electrolyte compatibility and post‐cycling characterization when evaluating antimony‐based materials for electrochemical energy storage.

title: Taguchi-based Optimization of Flanged Convergent-convergent Duct for Improving Micro Horizontal-axis Wind Turbine Performance
summary: A numerical optimization study was performed to determine an improved flanged converging–diverging duct geometry for enhancing the power performance of a micro horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT). The Taguchi method was employed for optimiz
content: A numerical optimization study was performed to determine an improved flanged converging–diverging duct geometry for enhancing the power performance of a micro horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT). The Taguchi method was employed for optimization. Five duct geometric parameters were considered control factors in the Taguchi method: the nozzle length, the nozzle angle, the diffuser angle, the flange length, and the flange angle. The optimization target was defined as the maximum rotor power coefficient (CP,max). Analysis of the Taguchi results revealed that the flange length exerted the most significant influence on CP,max among the investigated parameters. The optimum duct configuration achieved CP,max = 0.77 at 10 m/s and 0.76 at 16 m/s, respectively, representing increases of 48.4% and 71.4% compared with those of the worst duct configuration. In addition, the optimized duct accelerated the throat airflow velocity by 67.2% at 10 m/s and 65.5% at 16 m/s. With regard to the convergent nozzle in the duct, flow field analysis indicated that a smaller nozzle length and larger nozzle angle are favorable for accelerating the airflow. In addition, a longer flange with a flatter angle facilitates faster airflow movement through the wind turbine.

title: 11th International Engineering Conference on Emerging Trends in Engineering (IEC'2026)

summary: The eleventh International Engineering Conference (IEC’2026) will be held on April 29–30, 2026, under the theme “Innovative Engineering Research for Sustainable Development.” The event is jointly organized by the Faculty of Engineering at T
content: The eleventh International Engineering Conference (IEC’2026) will be held on April 29–30, 2026, under the theme “Innovative Engineering Research for Sustainable Development.” The event is jointly organized by the Faculty of Engineering at Tishk International University (TIU-Iraq), Erbil Polytechnic University (EPU-Iraq), and Nusa Putra University (Indonesia), with technical collaboration from IEEE and the IEEE Iraq Section. IEC’2026 provides a multidisciplinary forum for researchers, academics, and practitioners to present cutting-edge developments and advanced research across a wide spectrum of engineering disciplines. The conference covers key areas such as construction and structural engineering, structural materials, earthquake engineering, sustainable construction practices, composite materials, and construction management. It also addresses topics including environmental engineering, green and smart buildings, restoration and rehabilitation of historical structures, renewable energy systems, hydraulic engineering, sustainable materials, waste management, transportation engineering, and geotechnical engineering. In addition, emerging and rapidly evolving fields—such as surveying and geomatics engineering, highway engineering, data science, big data analytics, artificial intelligence, robotics, communications, and biomedical informatics—form an integral part of the conference program. The conference is supported by a program committee of 90 esteemed experts, approximately 85% of whom hold doctoral degrees in engineering disciplines aligned with the conference themes. All submitted papers undergo a rigorous double-blind peer review process, with each manuscript evaluated by at least three reviewers. The review process ensures that contributions meet essential criteria, including relevance, originality, timeliness, technical soundness, clarity of presentation, and appropriate use of references.The paper review process for IEC’2026 demonstrates a rigorous and well-structured evaluation across its co-located conferences and thematic tracks.
