title: Post-match biochemical signatures and their association with video tracking metrics in elite soccer (football) players using multiplatform targeted metabolomics
summary: Abstract Urinary metabolomics offers promise for monitoring exercise‑induced physiological stress in football, yet evidence linking post‑match urinary markers to match workload in elite players remains limited. This study investigated pre‑
content: Abstract Urinary metabolomics offers promise for monitoring exercise‑induced physiological stress in football, yet evidence linking post‑match urinary markers to match workload in elite players remains limited. This study investigated pre‑ to post‑match changes in the urinary metabolomic profile of professional male football players across 10 official matches, and examined their associations with external workload. A multiplatform targeted metabolomics workflow quantified 87 metabolites in 158 paired urine samples. External workload was characterized using a composite player load metric and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) of video tracking variables. Match‑play elicited a distinct urinary metabolomic shift, with 60 metabolites changing significantly. Orthogonal partial least square – discriminant analysis (OPLS‑DA) showed clear separation between pre‑ and post‑match samples. Urinary n-terminal titin fragment (UTF) exhibited large fold‑increases and the most consistent correlations with external workload indicators. Several short‑ and medium‑chain acylcarnitines, amino acid- and redox‑related metabolites, and purine‑related compounds also contributed to the post‑match metabolic signature, with some biomarkers showing statistically significant associations with workload metrics. Elite football match‑play is associated with a clear shift in the urinary metabolomic profile of professional male players. UTF emerged as the metabolite most closely linked to external workload, supporting its value as a as a practical tool for post‑match recovery monitoring.

title: TAMARINDUS INDICA PULP SUPPLEMENTATION IMPROVES SEMEN QUALITY AND OXIDATIVE RESISTANCE IN NOILER ROOSTERS DURING SHORT-TERM LIQUID STORAGE
source: Journal of Renewable Agricultural Technology Research
summary: This study evaluated the dose-dependent effects of tamarind (Tamarindus indica) pulp concentration (TPC) in drinking water on semen quality parameters of Noiler roosters under Sudan Savanna ecological conditions. Thirty-six sexually mature
content: This study evaluated the dose-dependent effects of tamarind (Tamarindus indica) pulp concentration (TPC) in drinking water on semen quality parameters of Noiler roosters under Sudan Savanna ecological conditions. Thirty-six sexually mature Noiler roosters were randomly assigned to four treatment groups (n=9 per group) in a completely randomized design: 0 (control), 5, 10, and 15 g TPC/L of drinking water. Semen was collected weekly over six weeks following a four-week adaptation period. Evaluated parameters included semen volume, pH, color, sperm motility, viability (live/dead ratio), morphology, and concentration, assessed both fresh and after short-term storage at 5°C for 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours. Tamarind pulp supplementation significantly (P < 0.05) enhanced semen quality in a dose-dependent manner. The 15 g/L treatment produced the highest semen volume (1.07 ± 0.05 mL), sperm motility (92.22 ± 1.69%), live sperm percentage (96.67 ± 0.88%), and normal morphology (95.00 ± 1.60%), representing improvements of 26%, 23%, 12%, and 15%, respectively, over the control. During storage, TPC-treated groups maintained superior sperm quality up to 6 hours, with the 15 g/L treatment preserving motility (5.25 ± 0.88%) and viability (9.50 ± 0.88%) compared to controls (2.50 ± 0.88% and 5.25 ± 0.88%, respectively). All treatments showed drastic quality decline beyond 12 hours of storage. Dietary tamarind pulp at 15 g/L of drinking water optimizes semen quality and short-term storage potential in Noiler roosters, likely through its antioxidant properties. This natural phytogenic additive offers a cost-effective strategy to enhance poultry reproductive performance in hot tropical environments, potentially improving fertility and hatchability in commercial and smallholder production systems.

title: Building Impact: A Scalable Model for Gender-Inclusive STEM Education
source: Proceedings of the Canadian Engineering Education Association (CEEA)
summary: Despite sustained national efforts to increase diversity in engineering, women remain underrepresented in many technology-focused disciplines. In response, a university-based summer STEM camp was established in 2017 to provide immersive eng
content: Despite sustained national efforts to increase diversity in engineering, women remain underrepresented in many technology-focused disciplines. In response, a university-based summer STEM camp was established in 2017 to provide immersive engineering experiences for girls aged 14 to 17. This study examines how structured summer STEM interventions influence participants’ interest in engineering, career intentions, and perceptions of gender equity. A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted across multiple cohorts from 2017 to 2025, drawing on data collected from 71 former camp participants. Quantitative findings indicate strengthened engineering interest, increased self-efficacy, and strong perceived program impact. Qualitative analysis reveals shifts in perceptions of belonging, representation, and accessibility, with hands-on design activities and mentorship identified as influential elements. Together, the findings suggest that structured and equity-informed outreach initiatives can support identity development and broaden participation in engineering pathways.

title: Solar Power Forecasting Using Deep Learning Model Based Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Method
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: Accurately forecasting solar power is essential for secure and efficient operations of contemporary power systems, particularly in the smart grid and renewable energy integration context. In this paper, we present a new hybrid deep learning
content: Accurately forecasting solar power is essential for secure and efficient operations of contemporary power systems, particularly in the smart grid and renewable energy integration context. In this paper, we present a new hybrid deep learning model, the BiLSTM Model using Improved PSO (BiLSTM-IPSO), for improved short-term prediction of solar power, which incorporates the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model with an Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) algorithm. The IPSO algorithm successively arranges the BiLSTM hyperparameters with chaotic initialization, adaptive inertia weights, and velocity clamping, to converge globally and avoid stagnating locally. The proposed BiLSTM-IPSO model performance is compared with various state-of-the-art techniques, including TLBO-DL, CNN-LBO, BiLSTM-AADC, and HCLN, using standard indicators, such as MSE, RMSE, MAE, MBE, and R². Results show that our model consistently performs better than all the baselines, and the lowest RMSE and the highest R² are 0.0565 and 0.955, respectively, on the 0.5-hour horizon. The excellent generalization performance of the framework in all of its forecast horizons indicates its feasibility for applications in real-time deployment in solar energy management systems and smart-grid operations.

title: An Artificial Intelligence Model for Corporate Financial Strategy and Sustainable Global Business Growth
source: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
summary: In an era of increasing global economic complexity, corporations face unprecedented challenges in aligning financial strategy with sustainable business growth. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) model designed to enhance co
content: In an era of increasing global economic complexity, corporations face unprecedented challenges in aligning financial strategy with sustainable business growth. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) model designed to enhance corporate financial strategy by integrating predictive analytics, real-time data processing, and advanced decision-support frameworks. The model leverages machine learning algorithms to forecast revenues, optimize capital allocation, and assess risk exposure across multiple operational and market scenarios. By providing accurate, dynamic, and actionable financial insights, the AI framework enables organizations to make informed strategic decisions, enhance operational efficiency, and anticipate market shifts proactively. The study emphasizes the role of AI in promoting sustainability, highlighting how predictive financial planning can align corporate objectives with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations while supporting long-term value creation.

title: Energy diversification and sustainable development: insights from G20 countries
source: International Journal of Energy Sector Management
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of energy diversification on sustainable development for G20 countries. The study uses different proxies of energy diversification to examine this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using
content: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of energy diversification on sustainable development for G20 countries. The study uses different proxies of energy diversification to examine this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using a balanced panel data set for G20 countries from 2000 to 2021, based on data availability. The dependent variable is sustainable development, whereas the independent variables are the three constructed indices. The study uses linear (feasible generalized least squares, panel-corrected standard error, Driscoll−Kraay standard error) as well as nonlinear (method of moments quantile regression and bootstrap quantile regression) models and GMM to check the impact of the energy diversification on sustainable development. Findings This study finds that energy diversification helps in achieving sustainable development across the three developed energy diversification indices, so increasing the infusion of cleaner energy sources helps countries to achieve sustainable development. Originality/value This study constructs three different energy diversification indices to examine the impact of energy diversification on sustainable development in G20 countries, which play a vital role in the sustainable development of the global economy, highlighting that increased infusion of renewable energy sources in the overall energy mix plays a vital role in the path toward sustainability.

title: PRODUCTIVE WAQF AND THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS: POLICY AND INSTITUTIONAL CHALLENGES IN LOCAL WAQF DEVELOPMENT IN INDONESIA
summary: This study examines why the transformation of traditional waqf into productive waqf remains limited in Indonesia despite its significant potential and explores its relevance for supporting sustainable development at the local level. This st
content: This study examines why the transformation of traditional waqf into productive waqf remains limited in Indonesia despite its significant potential and explores its relevance for supporting sustainable development at the local level. This study employed a qualitative case study approach in Palopo City, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, including nazhir, officials from the Ministry of Religious Affairs, mosque administrators, religious leaders, and community representatives. Field observations and document analysis of waqf regulations, institutional reports, and policy documents were also conducted. The findings reveal that most waqf assets in Palopo are still utilized for traditional religious purposes such as mosques, prayer rooms, schools, and cemeteries, while productive utilization remains limited. Major barriers include the absence of specialized waqf institutions, limited managerial capacity among nazhir, weak institutional coordination, and dominant traditional perceptions of waqf within the community. Informal and familial patterns in the appointment of nazhir further constrain professional governance and productive asset management. Nevertheless, emerging initiatives, such as the use of mosque waqf land for micro-enterprise rentals, illustrate the potential of productive waqf to support local economic empowerment and social welfare. Although limited to a single local context, this study offers practical implications for the Indonesian Waqf Board, the Ministry of Religious Affairs, local governments, mosque committees, and nazhir development programs by underscoring the need for stronger coordination and professional capacity in productive waqf management. This study contributes local empirical evidence by highlighting the gap between national waqf policies and local implementation while demonstrating the potential contribution of productive waqf to community-based development aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Sparse Component-Driven Deep Voiceprint Feature Modeling and Intelligent Identification Method for Transformer Mechanical Faults
source: International Journal of Information Technologies and Systems Approach
summary: Aiming at the difficult problem of transformer mechanical fault detection, this article aims to build an efficient and accurate identification model to ensure the stable operation of an electric power system. First, the principle of transfo
content: Aiming at the difficult problem of transformer mechanical fault detection, this article aims to build an efficient and accurate identification model to ensure the stable operation of an electric power system. First, the principle of transformer mechanical fault and the characteristics of voiceprint are described in detail. On this basis, sparse component analysis is combined with deep learning technology to realize sparse component-driven deep voiceprint feature modeling. Specifically, extensive transformer voiceprint data are collected by building an experimental platform. Using sparse component analysis, the voiceprint features are accurately extracted, and fault identification is carried out with the help of a mixed deep learning model combining a convolutional neural network and long short-term memory network. After many experiments, the model effectively suppressed the overfitting phenomenon in the training stage.

title: Analisis Proses Diagnosis Kerusakan Clutch Kompresor AC Mobil Nissan X-Trail T30 Menggunakan Scanner Universal
source: Mars Jurnal Teknik Mesin Industri Elektro Dan Ilmu Komputer
summary: This study analyzed an open-circuit fault in the air-conditioning compressor-clutch circuit of a Nissan X-Trail T30 using a universal OBD-II scanner and a digital multimeter. The vehicle exhibited a non-cooling condition: the blower and A/C
content: This study analyzed an open-circuit fault in the air-conditioning compressor-clutch circuit of a Nissan X-Trail T30 using a universal OBD-II scanner and a digital multimeter. The vehicle exhibited a non-cooling condition: the blower and A/C indicator operated, but the compressor clutch did not engage. The diagnosis was conducted sequentially from the control request to the actuator response. Scanner data confirmed communication with the engine control module and an accepted A/C request. Electrical measurements confirmed that the 10 A A/C fuse, relay supply, relay contact, and voltage at A/C relay E5 terminal 5 were normal. However, battery voltage was absent at compressor connector E34 terminal 1, and continuity testing between E5 terminal 5 and E34 terminal 1 indicated an open circuit (OL). Direct battery activation produced an engagement click, confirming that the magnetic clutch remained functional. After repair of the cable or connector, continuity and supply voltage at E34 were restored and the clutch operated normally. All measurements relevant to the electrical-diagnosis objective were completed and reported categorically according to Nissan service-manual criteria, covering voltage availability, continuity status, and clutch response. The findings show that scanner information must be combined with voltage, continuity, and direct-actuation tests to localize electrical faults and prevent unnecessary compressor replacement.

title: ‘Scale Quantum, not bureaucracy’
summary: The emerging ‘quantum era’ is often framed in terms of technological revolution and geopolitical competition. This paper offers a more grounded account of the development of quantum technologies by examining their formal standardization pro
content: The emerging ‘quantum era’ is often framed in terms of technological revolution and geopolitical competition. This paper offers a more grounded account of the development of quantum technologies by examining their formal standardization processes. Focusing on two key institutional sites—CEN-CENELEC JTC 22 and IEC/ISO JTC 3—we analyze how actors negotiate and stabilize meanings, priorities, and responsibilities in this early and uncertain technological field. Drawing on the theoretical framework of policy logics, we identify three dynamics that shape quantum standardization: (1) technological uncertainty and the premature timing of standardization complicate institutional coordination and national strategy; (2) conflicting policy logics are fused to ‘infrastructure’ an institutional formation that acquires autonomy over time; and (3) formal standards processes serve as a pressure valve for geopolitical tensions surrounding global technological trajectories. The analysis builds on a year-long ethnography of standardization meetings and plenaries, complemented by 9 elite interviews. By bridging insights from science and technology studies, institutional theory, and international political economy, the paper demonstrates how standardization institutions mediate the governance and global politics of emerging technologies.

title: The Relevance of Green Criminology in Criminal Law
summary: This study examines the integration of green criminology into Indonesia's correctional system as a response to environmental challenges and the limitations of conventional rehabilitation models. Using a qualitative approach, it explores how
content: This study examines the integration of green criminology into Indonesia's correctional system as a response to environmental challenges and the limitations of conventional rehabilitation models. Using a qualitative approach, it explores how an ecocentric perspective can transform correctional institutions from punitive facilities into sustainable rehabilitation systems. The findings indicate that integrating ecological values through urban farming, waste recycling, and energy conservation programs promotes environmental restoration while supporting inmates' social reintegration and psychological well-being. Article 85 of the Indonesian Criminal Code provides a legal basis for implementing ecological restorative justice, although its application remains constrained by limited infrastructure, funding, and institutional capacity. The study identifies Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) and Community-Based Corrections (CBC) as promising mechanisms for strengthening rehabilitation through environmentally sustainable initiatives and circular economy practices. Overall, the findings suggest that green criminology provides a practical framework for developing a correctional system that is adaptive, ecologically just, and responsive to Indonesia's evolving socio-environmental challenges.

title: Operational regime dependence of model performance and feature importance in machine learning-based gas turbine power prediction
summary: Industrial gas turbines play a vital role in modern power generation, providing flexible and efficient power generation that supports grid stability as renewable energy penetration increases. While machine learning has been widely applied t
content: Industrial gas turbines play a vital role in modern power generation, providing flexible and efficient power generation that supports grid stability as renewable energy penetration increases. While machine learning has been widely applied to gas turbine power prediction, existing studies typically evaluate models over a single, mixed operating regime and do not examine how feature importance and model rankings change once transient and steady-state operation are distinguished. This study addresses that gap using approximately two years of real industrial operational data from a continuously monitored gas turbine, comparing Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and an Artificial Neural Network on both the original, mixed-regime dataset and a physically motivated, steady-state filtered subset (Fuel Flow Rate ≥ 65 KPPH, equivalent to 8.19 kg/s). On the original dataset, ANN and Random Forest achieved the best performance (RMSE = 3.94–3.97 MW), while Linear Regression performed substantially worse (RMSE = 46.7 MW) due to a pronounced nonlinear idle-to-operating transition. The ranking reverses when steady-state operation is isolated, with Linear Regression achieving the lowest error of all four models (RMSE = 1.74 MW, versus 2.14–3.69 MW for the nonlinear models). This regime-dependent reversal has not previously been reported in the gas turbine literature. SHAP-based feature importance further reveals that the four models show substantial disagreement regarding the dominant predictor under mixed conditions (individual model shares ranging from 19.1% to 75.1%, spanning turbine outlet temperature, fuel flow rate, and compressor exit pressure depending on architecture) but converge consistently on compressor exit pressure (45.2–82.7% of total SHAP importance across all four models) once steady-state operation is isolated, a convergence explained here through a quantitative variance-collapse mechanism rather than asserted qualitatively. A progressive feature elimination analysis further shows that, under steady-state conditions, a minimal one to three-feature model is not merely sufficient but measurably outperforms the full feature set (RMSE ≈ 2.6 MW versus 3.55 MW), an actionable finding for reduced-sensor deployments. These results demonstrate that both model selection and feature interpretation in gas turbine power prediction are fundamentally regime-dependent, providing a physically grounded framework for reliable, interpretable, and deployable predictive models in industrial gas turbine systems. The methods themselves are standard; the novelty lies in the paired original-versus-filtered comparison design, which reveals regime-dependent behavior invisible to the single-regime evaluations common in prior gas turbine studies.

title: Mobile money, and the welfare of women and youths in fragile states: Evidence from Mozambique
summary: Mobile money has emerged as a low-cost financial instrument with strong potential to improve livelihoods, particularly in economies with weak formal financial systems. This paper examines the welfare effects on women and youth in Mozambique
content: Mobile money has emerged as a low-cost financial instrument with strong potential to improve livelihoods, particularly in economies with weak formal financial systems. This paper examines the welfare effects on women and youth in Mozambique, a fragile, post-conflict country exposed to climate shocks. Using 900 household observations from the 2019 FinScope Survey and an instrumental variable approach to address selection bias, the study provides robust evidence on welfare outcomes. Results show that mobile money improves household welfare, with effects driven by active usage rather than mere account ownership. Specifically, mobile money reduces reliance on own food production, indicating improved market integration and liquidity, while enhancing consumption smoothing and investment in human capital. Welfare gains are transmitted through remittances and financial inclusion, strengthening household resilience. Women benefit through increased financial autonomy, consistent with evidence that digital financial services improve women's entrepreneurship, financial decision-making, and economic empowerment [33], while youth rely on remittances to stabilize consumption. However, the instrumental variable approach relies on the assumption that network availability affects welfare only through mobile money adoption, a claim that cannot be fully tested and should be interpreted with caution. These findings suggest that policies should prioritize active usage and ecosystem integration over access alone.

title: PLANtoACT Task 2.1: Hourly profiles - Heating and cooling demand
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Regional Heating and Cooling Demand Profiles for the PLANtoACT Project This dataset contains normalized hourly heating and cooling demand profiles developed for the PLANtoACT project (Task 2.2). The profiles represent the long-term building
content: Regional Heating and Cooling Demand Profiles for the PLANtoACT Project This dataset contains normalized hourly heating and cooling demand profiles developed for the PLANtoACT project (Task 2.2). The profiles represent the long-term building heating and cooling demand behaviour of five European pilot regions and are intended for use in energy system modelling, renewable energy assessment, and regional energy planning. The dataset was generated using the Renewables.ninja weather API together with the demand_ninja building energy demand model and regional administrative boundaries. Hourly weather data (temperature, global horizontal radiation, humidity, wind speed) were downloaded for MERRA-2 grid points located within each region, converted into hourly heating and cooling demand, averaged into a representative regional profile, and normalized while preserving the long-term degree-hour equivalent — the demand-side analogue of the equivalent full-load hours used for the wind, solar, and hydro generation profiles. The dataset accompanies the scripts available in the corresponding GitLab repository. title: Reliability-Informed Life Prediction for New Energy Vehicle Components
source: Journal of Intelligence and Engineering Technology
summary: For new energy vehicle components, remaining service life requires crucial maintenance, but operating conditions and incomplete fault records still limit the sustainable development of models. This study constructs a data-driven framework f
content: For new energy vehicle components, remaining service life requires crucial maintenance, but operating conditions and incomplete fault records still limit the sustainable development of models. This study constructs a data-driven framework for batteries and traction motors by integrating fault analysis, reliability parameter estimation, and machine learning-based prediction. This framework can support maintenance planning and spare parts planning to some extent. However, these results should be interpreted with caution because component type, brand coverage, and data quality may introduce unobserved biases. More extensive cross-brand datasets, prediction ranges that account for uncertainty, and real-time validation are needed before reliable large-scale deployment.
